profile.name: Zaki Akdas Choudhary
profile.headline: Crafting stellar digital experiences
profile.tagline: I design and build fast, immersive, 3D-animated websites and web apps that turn first-time visitors into paying clients.
profile.about: I'm Zaki Akdas Choudhary, a software developer with a BCA (IT) background who lives at the intersection of engineering and art. I help startups, studios and founders ship products that don't just work — they feel alive. My specialty is combining rock-solid full-stack architecture with real-time 3D, motion design and obsessive performance tuning.
profile.aboutMore: When I'm not pushing pixels through a GPU, I'm writing about WebGL performance, contributing to open source, or mentoring junior developers. I work with clients worldwide, remote-first, and I treat every project like a mission launch: clear plan, tight feedback loops, zero surprises.

posts.title: Making WebGL fly on mid-range Android phones
posts.excerpt: Most 3D websites die on a Pixel 6a. Here is the exact playbook I use to keep 60fps on the phones your real visitors actually own.
posts.content:
Every client asks for a site that *wows*. Nobody asks for a site that wows **only on a MacBook Pro** — but that is what most 3D portfolios deliver.

Here is the playbook I use on every WebGL project.

## 1. Budget your pixels, not your polygons

On mobile, fill-rate kills you long before vertex count does. The single biggest win is capping device pixel ratio:

```js
<Canvas dpr={[1, 1.5]} />
```

A phone with DPR 3 renders **4x fewer pixels** at DPR 1.5. Nobody notices the difference on a 6-inch screen. Everybody notices 22fps.

## 2. Feature-detect, then degrade gracefully

- Check `navigator.hardwareConcurrency` — 4 cores or fewer gets the lite scene
- Check for WebGL2, fall back to a CSS starfield if missing
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` — accessibility is not optional

## 3. Kill postprocessing on mobile

Bloom and depth-of-field are full-screen passes. On a 750-wide phone they can cost more than your entire scene. Fake bloom with additive-blended sprites instead — it is close to free.

## 4. Instance everything that repeats

My asteroid belt renders 420 rocks in **one draw call** with InstancedMesh. The naive version was 420 draw calls. Frame time went from 11ms to 1.3ms.

## 5. Test on the phone your users own

Not your iPhone 15 Pro. A three-year-old mid-ranger. If it runs there, it runs everywhere.

> The wow factor is worthless if half your visitors bounce before it loads.
posts.metaTitle: WebGL Performance on Mid-Range Android — Field Guide
posts.metaDescription: A practical playbook for keeping 3D websites at 60fps on the phones real users own: DPR caps, feature detection, instancing and graceful degradation.

posts.title: Case study: how a 3D configurator lifted conversion 34%
posts.excerpt: The full story behind Nebula Commerce — why the old store failed, what we built instead, and the numbers after 90 days.
posts.content:
Nebula Audio came to me with a template store and a problem: **2.1% conversion on desktop, 0.8% on mobile**, for a premium product that photographs beautifully.

## The diagnosis

Their product pages looked like every competitor. Static gallery, spec table, buy button. For a 300-dollar headphone, buyers need to *feel* the product — and photos were not doing it.

## What we built

- A real-time 3D product configurator (React Three Fiber) — rotate, zoom, change colourways and materials live
- Edge-cached product pages with Next.js — TTFB under 100ms worldwide
- One-page checkout with Stripe Payment Element

## The constraints that mattered

1. The 3D model had to load in under 1.5 seconds on 4G — we Draco-compressed the GLB from 8.4MB to 640KB
2. Mobile had to keep 60fps — baked lighting, one directional light, DPR capped at 1.5
3. SEO could not suffer — all product copy stays in server-rendered HTML, the canvas is purely additive

## Results after 90 days

- Conversion: 2.1% → **2.8% desktop**, 0.8% → **1.4% mobile** (+34% blended)
- Average session time on product pages: **4.2x longer**
- Support tickets asking about colour options: down 61%

> Takeaway: 3D is not decoration. Done right, it answers buying questions that photos cannot.
posts.metaDescription: How a real-time 3D product configurator built with React Three Fiber lifted e-commerce conversion by 34% in 90 days.
